BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package vs Buyer Playbook

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from the playbook on almost every material point. Several items, including the 20% cap, the 18-month period, and the Bluefen and Riverlark mechanics, sit at or beyond our conditional fallbacks. Under the playbook, no fallback can be offered without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. **Nothing in the Seller's package should be accepted or signalled as acceptable in the mark-up.** The Seller's summary is also silent on fraud carve-outs, so the SPA text needs checking clause by clause. I have reviewed the summary and disclosure letter only, not the full draft SPA.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only as fallback with Frost's written authority | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20%. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Reject. Counter at 24 months. |
| Limitation cross-application (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. Delete the default-to-all wording. |
| Fundamental/Title (summary) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum enforceable extent, non-waivable | Reject. Insert a fraud carve-out; confirm it is in the SPA text. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room (to 22 Sept 2026, DD-002 to DD-012) and public registers deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject deemed disclosure of the data room and public registers. Require specific disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. This clause would undercut almost every specific issue in the disclosure letter. |
| Bluefen consent (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of written consent | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are met before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Make effective consent plus evidence of Clause 11.3 conditions a condition precedent. DL 2 confirms no final consent yet. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m facility released "following Completion" | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Reject. Require a payoff letter and repayment from Completion funds. DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included. |
| Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised | Specific line item or seller-funded, with triggered on-costs | Reject silent exclusion. Require a specific line item or seller funding, and quantify on-costs. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject "adequate". Broaden the indemnity; verify the AUD 180,000 independently. |
| DD-006 export incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion. Require log preservation, investigation scope and regular updates. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course" costs | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation. Request contracts and assess. Test whether the three renewals are one arrangement split up (DL 8 says read together). |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Reject. Keep Tax and IP as separate open categories. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source only | Reject as sole evidence. See verification list below. |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. Caps, thresholds and time limits are at or past our fallbacks.** The Seller has taken our conditional fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months) as its opening position and tightened the thresholds to five times our basket. Together the de minimis and excess-only basket would sharply reduce recoverable general claims. The mark-up should restore our starting positions and should not signal that a fallback exists.

**2. Fundamental/Title and the general regime.** Folding title and capacity into the general regime would let the general cap, basket, time limit and knowledge bar cut into claims that go to whether the Buyer actually owns what it is paying for. The playbook treats this as non-negotiable.

**3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge work together.** The Seller's disclosure letter discloses the whole data room, and clause 8.3 bars claims about anything discoverable there. Read together, the Buyer would lose claims on the very issues flagged in the disclosure letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the incident). The disclosure letter's date also needs a bring-down: it speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.

**4. Completion-critical items are not conditions.** Bluefen (about 30% of FY26 revenue, AUD 3.6m) and Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) are both unresolved. The Seller proposes to handle them through deemed satisfaction or post-Completion release. Both should be conditions precedent or funded at Completion.

**5. Funds flow.** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 are outside the draft funds flow, and their on-costs are unquantified. Silent exclusion would shift a known liability to the Buyer. The playbook requires a specific line item or Seller funding.

## Verification and gaps to close

- **Title:** current ASIC company extract, register of members, share certificates, PPSR and other encumbrance searches (including whether Riverlark security extends to the shares), and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell. DD-012 alone is not sufficient.
- **Bluefen:** the executed consent, and evidence that every Clause 11.3 condition is satisfied.
- **Riverlark:** a payoff letter and draft discharge documents.
- **Ironquay:** bank or counterparty evidence on the AUD 180,000 and on SOW3 payment status; the transfer documents for Project Materials.
- **Bonuses:** the DD-005 calculation of on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation).
- **DD-006:** the logs, the investigation scope, and the Privacy Act assessment (including whether any notification obligation applies). Privacy counsel should review this.
- **Sandbar:** the three renewal contracts, their terms, termination rights and timing.
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** whether landlord or Mossvale consent or notice is required by reason of the share sale. The Seller's disclosure says only "notification" and "restriction on assignment". Treat any consent requirement as a condition.
- **SPA text:** confirm the fraud carve-out, governing law (NSW), and the exact wording of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as a whole** and send a mark-up restoring playbook positions: 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, 24-month general period.
2. **Do not offer or signal fallbacks.** The 20% cap and 18-month period require Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None exists.
3. **Separate the regimes:** Title and capacity at 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar; Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept separate with no general-regime override.
4. **Insert a non-waivable fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Delete deemed disclosure** of the data room and public registers; require specific disclosure; bring the disclosure letter down to current date.
6. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar** (8.3).
7. **Make Bluefen a condition precedent:** effective consent plus evidence of conditions. No consent-on-delivery, no reasonable endeavours.
8. **Riverlark:** payoff letter, repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Any post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3 while preserving the cure; verify the AUD 180,000.
11. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation, and updates. Do not accept "not material" or assume a breach either way.
12. **Sandbar:** obtain contracts and assess. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open. Do not accept "settled under the general regime".
14. **Title:** require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm whether consent is required; if so, make it a condition.

Two caveats. First, this is a playbook-based review of the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not of the full SPA text, so each clause needs checking against the actual drafting. Second, the privacy notification analysis and the Australian tax and employment on-cost questions should go to specialist NSW and Australian counsel before any position is taken with the Seller.
